story.title: The Night Someone Shouted Land
story.story: The sailors had stared at empty ocean for more than five weeks. Some of them wanted to turn back. Then, people say, a lookout named Rodrigo shouted that he saw land. It was the night of October eleventh, fourteen ninety-two. Columbus was certain he had reached Asia, the land of spices and silk. He was wrong about that. But the island was real, and people already lived there. They were the Taíno, and they came down to the sand to meet the strangers. Columbus named the island and raised a flag. Then the ships sailed on among the islands. When they finally saw Spain again, the sailors had a story no one in Europe had heard.

claims.claim: The sailors had been at sea for more than five weeks before land was sighted.
Some of the sailors wanted to turn back before land was sighted.
A lookout named Rodrigo de Triana is credited with first sighting land.
Land was sighted on the night of October 11, 1492.
Columbus believed he had reached Asia.
The island was inhabited by the Taíno people, who met the Europeans on the beach.
Columbus named the island and raised a flag there.
The expedition returned to Spain and brought news of the lands to Europe.

issues.description: The story says 'Columbus was certain he had reached Asia.' The ledger only supports that he 'believed' he had reached Asia. 'Certain' describes his inner state more strongly than the ledger does.
